minutes.headline: Select Board told the preservation commissions it plans to seek demolition of the old primary school for a town green.
minutes.summary: After routine items (a Dunkin' license transfer, two DPW hire ratifications, minutes, warrants, town manager report), the board held a joint workshop with the Architectural Preservation District Commission and Historical Commission on the vacant old primary school. The board said it will bring a Town Meeting article for green space design and later demolition; the APDC objected and asked for a wider RFP or lease effort. The chair agreed to consider a lease-only RFP at a future meeting; no vote was taken on the building.

what_happened.line: The Select Board told the Architectural Preservation District and Historical Commissions it intends to seek demolition of the old primary school for a green space.
The board plans a Town Meeting article for green space design money first, with a demolition request to follow; no vote was taken on the building.
The chair said the board will consider a lease-only RFP for the old primary school at a future meeting; the preservation commission members are to send the town manager what they want in it.
The board approved a common victualler license for Dippin Donuts, 4-0 on roll call as heard.
The board ratified the town manager's two DPW appointments, an intermittent heavy equipment operator and a heavy equipment operator.

why_it_matters: The old primary school's future, demolition for a green space or a lease to a new user, will likely come to residents as a Town Meeting article, with costs paid by the town budget, mostly taxes.
The board said green space costs far less than renovating the building, but no current estimate was presented, so residents have no up-to-date cost comparison.
watch_next: A future Select Board agenda item on a lease-only RFP for the old primary school.
The Feb 2 or Feb 9 meeting, where a review of the APDC bylaw as it applies to town property is to be tried.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the warrant totals, the $80,000 fuel tank figure and the green space design article, and most attendee differences are misspelled names. They differ on the votes: our minutes record a roll-call license vote and four-member votes, while the official minutes record neither the license nor a four-member count. Our minutes also carry decisions the official minutes lack: the lease-only RFP, the Jeffries bylaw review and the $500,000 demolition estimate.
